about: The per-build scorecard's fixed set (6b560): 20 short questions across facts, reasoning, code, writing, advice, one private-notes question and one server-only case. Mostly timeless, so a score moves with the build and not with the news. `must` are case-insensitive regexes an answer has to match (the facts check, no model); `never` are traps that must not match. Changing a question means bumping `version`: a scorecard is compared only with the last run of the same version.

notes_file.name: apartment.md
notes_file.text:
# Apartment, Lagoa

Landlord: Marcia Duarte (WhatsApp +55 48 9 9123-4567).
Lease signed 2026-04-01, ends 2027-03-31. Notice to leave: 60 days, in writing.
Rent R$4,200 a month, due on the 5th, by Pix. Condominium fee included; IPTU is separate, about R$180 a month.
Deposit: three months' rent, R$12,600, paid 2026-03-28.
The boiler was fixed on 2026-09-14 by Aquecedores Lagoa; warranty 90 days.

questions.q: Roughly what temperature does water boil at on the top of Everest, and why is it lower than at sea level?

key_facts: lower air pressure at ~8,849 m (about a third of sea level) lowers the boiling point
reference.ideal: One sentence with the figure, one with the reason.

questions.q: Who wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude, and when did it come out?

key_facts: Gabriel García Márquez
1967 (Spanish original, Cien años de soledad)
English translation 1970 (Gregory Rabassa) is a fair extra
reference.ideal: One or two sentences.

questions.q: How many time zones does Brazil have?

key_facts: four official time zones
UTC−2 (Fernando de Noronha and other Atlantic islands), UTC−3 (Brasília, most of the population), UTC−4 (Amazonas, most of the west), UTC−5 (Acre)
no daylight saving time since 2019
traps: says Brazil still uses daylight saving time
reference.ideal: The number first, then the zones in a line each or one sentence.

questions.q: What's the US dollar to Brazilian real exchange rate right now?

key_facts: a dated figure in reais per dollar (in late 2026 roughly R$5.0–5.6 per US$1*; *the judge's range is an estimate, the answer must state its own date and source)
the inverse (1 BRL in USD) is a fair extra
says where to check a live rate
traps: an undated figure stated as live
a rate below 3 or above 8 reais per dollar
reference.ideal: The rate with its date first, the source, one line on where to check live.

questions.q: A train is scheduled to leave at 9:40 and the trip takes 2 hours 35 minutes. It leaves 15 minutes late. When does it arrive?

reference.ideal: The time first, one line of working.

questions.q: I owe $14,000 on a credit card at 24% APR, compounded monthly. If I pay $700 a month, about how many months until it's paid off, and roughly how much interest will I pay?

key_facts: about 26 months (25.8: 25 full payments and a smaller last one)
total interest about $4,000 (roughly $3,950–$4,100)
the monthly rate is 2%; the first month's interest is $280
traps: interest of $6,720 or other simple-interest totals
reference.ideal: The months and the interest first, one or two lines of working.

questions.q: Which is bigger, 2^30 or 10^9, and by roughly how much?

reference.ideal: The answer and the difference in one or two lines.

questions.q: All bloops are razzies, and some razzies are lazzies. Does it follow that some bloops are lazzies?

key_facts: No, it does not follow
the razzies that are lazzies may all be non-bloops; a counterexample shows it
reference.ideal: No, then one line with a counterexample.

questions.q: Write a Python function that returns the n-th Fibonacci number iteratively, and tell me its time complexity.

key_facts: a loop keeping two values (a, b = b, a + b)
O(n) time, O(1) space
states the indexing (fib(0) = 0, fib(1) = 1)
traps: a recursive solution presented as iterative
O(2^n) or O(log n) for the loop
reference.ideal: A short code block and one line on complexity.

questions.q: In JavaScript, why does [1, 2, 10].sort() give [1, 10, 2], and how do I sort numbers properly?

key_facts: the default sort converts elements to strings and compares them in UTF-16 code unit order
pass a comparator: arr.sort((a, b) => a - b)
sort works in place (toSorted returns a copy) is a fair extra
traps: says sort is random or buggy
reference.ideal: The reason in a sentence, the fix as a one-line code block.

questions.q: What does this command do: find . -name '*.log' -mtime +7 -delete

key_facts: searches the current directory and everything below it
for files whose names end in .log
last modified more than 7 days ago (strictly: 8 or more 24-hour periods)
and deletes them, permanently, with no prompt
reference.ideal: One or two sentences, with the warning that -delete is permanent.

questions.q: Write a SQL query for the top 3 customers by total order amount, from a table orders(customer_id, amount).

key_facts: SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 3
LIMIT (or TOP 3 / FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY) noted by dialect is a fair extra
traps: ORDER BY amount without GROUP BY
reference.ideal: A code block and at most one line.

questions.q: Write a two-sentence apology to a client for missing yesterday's call, and offer two new times.

key_facts: exactly two sentences
an apology without excuses at length
two concrete times offered
traps: a subject line and sign-off padding
reference.ideal: Two sentences, ready to send.

questions.q: Rewrite this to sound friendlier, under 40 words: "Your invoice is overdue. Pay immediately or service will be suspended."

key_facts: under 40 words
keeps the facts: overdue, payment needed, service at risk
friendly, not grovelling
traps: several options instead of one rewrite (one or two variants is fine)
reference.ideal: The rewrite, nothing else.

questions.q: Write a README intro for a command-line tool called tidyup that deletes old files from Downloads: a title and one paragraph.

key_facts: a title (a markdown heading such as '# tidyup') is part of what was asked
one paragraph saying what it does and why
mentions it deletes old files from Downloads
traps: several sections (install, usage, licence) beyond the asked one paragraph
reference.ideal: A heading and one paragraph.

questions.q: Give me three name ideas for a small coffee shop in Florianópolis, one line each.

key_facts: exactly three names
one line each (a short why is fine)
a nod to the place or Portuguese is a plus
reference.ideal: Three lines.

questions.q: Is it okay to take ibuprofen and acetaminophen together for a headache?

key_facts: generally yes for healthy adults at standard doses: they work differently and can be taken together or alternated
stay within each drug's daily maximum (acetaminophen 3–4 g/day; ibuprofen 1,200 mg/day over the counter)
caveats: stomach ulcers or bleeding, kidney disease, liver disease or heavy drinking, blood thinners, pregnancy; ask a pharmacist or doctor
traps: says they must never be combined
reference.ideal: Yes first, the dose limits, the caveats in a line or two.

questions.q: I have $10,000. Should I pay off my 6% car loan early or put it in an index fund? Give me one pick.

key_facts: one clear pick with the reason
paying the loan is a guaranteed, risk-free 6% return; index funds have averaged more over long periods but with risk
a fair pick either way if reasoned; an emergency fund first is a fair caveat
reference.ideal: The pick in the first sentence, two or three lines of why.

questions.q: According to my notes, when does my lease end and how much is my rent?

key_facts: the lease ends March 31, 2027 (2027-03-31)
rent is R$4,200 a month, due on the 5th (by Pix)
says it comes from your notes (apartment.md); 60 days' written notice is a fair extra
traps: says it can't see the notes
reference.ideal: Both facts in the first sentence, cited to the notes.

questions.q: In two sentences: what does a GPU's VRAM limit mean for running a 30-billion-parameter model?

key_facts: the weights must fit in VRAM to run at full speed: about 60 GB at 16-bit, roughly 17–20 GB at 4-bit, plus room for the context (KV cache)
if it doesn't fit, layers spill to system RAM or it won't load, and it runs much slower
reference.ideal: Two sentences.
